summary: Full backend + frontend verification of the new OTA feature (backend firmware/upload, firmware/latest, firmware/download) and the two frontend surfaces that consume them (RadarCard on Summary + hidden Device Info 'Latest firmware' row). All 11 pytest cases pass (3 regression + 8 OTA) and every UI check from the review request passes on the mobile web preview at 390x844. Fresh-store contract (available=false, update=false, download 404) verified by physically clearing /app/backend/fw_store/ before the run. Post-upload contract verified: available=true, update=true when current is older, update=false when current matches, download returns application/octet-stream with byte-identical payload. Tiny (<1000B) upload correctly rejected with HTTP 400. Frontend: 'Sky right now' + RadarCard are absent before a ZIP is set (Charlotte 28117 placeholder only — no lat/lon yet), then appear on Summary after entering ZIP 10001 on the Flights tab; RainViewer + ESRI tiles rendered a real map with the location marker. Tapping the radar opens the fullscreen 'Live Radar' modal (pinch/pan/reset/play controls all render) and the close X returns cleanly to Summary. The 7-tap easter egg on the Device tab footer reveals the Device Info card which now shows the new 'Latest firmware' row displaying 'v1.2.0' (the value uploaded during backend OTA testing) — proving the /api/firmware/latest fetch on that screen works end-to-end. The 'Install update over Wi-Fi' PrimaryButton correctly does NOT render on web (BLE is native-only, connected===false), which matches the design. Note per the request: fw_store now contains a small test binary (v1.2.0, 1613 bytes) left in place intentionally.
action_items: No functional fixes required — all OTA endpoints and UI surfaces behave per the spec.
Optional hardening (carry-over from iteration_26, not blocking): _fetch_temp still has no custom User-Agent and _feed_cache is still unbounded — cosmetic only.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py now ~340 lines (still under the 700 threshold) but is fanning out into three distinct domains (status CRUD, matrix feed proxy, firmware OTA). Consider splitting into /app/backend/routers/{status,matrix_feed,firmware}.py before it gets larger.

firmware_upload writes the .bin under _FW_DIR without any per-request auth or size ceiling (only a 1000-byte floor). Fine for a private ESP32 fleet, but if the preview URL is ever public an attacker could fill disk. Consider (a) an upper size cap (e.g. 4MB is well over an ESP32 partition), (b) a simple shared-secret header check, or (c) rate limiting.

firmware_latest returns url='/api/firmware/download' as a relative path; the ESP32 needs the caller to know the origin. Not a bug (device.tsx concatenates base + url), just document it. On the frontend fetch, EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL is used correctly.

device.tsx line 108: the /api/firmware/latest fetch has no error/loading UI state (only setFwLatest(null) on failure). The row falls back to 'none uploaded' which conflates 'nothing uploaded' with 'network error' — minor UX, worth an inline error affordance if reachable.

device.tsx: firmwareVersion is used both as caller current for OTA check and as displayed 'Firmware'. When BLE is disconnected on web this is null so `current=` is empty — server correctly treats empty as needing an update. This is consistent.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_firmware_ota.py (new — 3 regression + 8 OTA pytest cases with autouse fixture that clears fw_store before the run)
seed_data_creation: Backend OTA test uploads a 1613-byte test firmware with version='1.2.0' to /app/backend/fw_store/. Per the review-request context note, this test binary is intentionally left in place after the run so the Device Info 'Latest firmware' row keeps rendering 'v1.2.0'. status_checks collection also has one TEST_matrix_feed_regression row left over from iteration_26 (no destructive endpoint exists).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend base URL EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL=https://smart-matrix-hub.preview.emergentagent.com; /health is un-prefixed and must be hit at http://localhost:8001/health. Firmware store lives at /app/backend/fw_store/ (files firmware.bin, meta.json). The autouse _clear_fw_store fixture in test_firmware_ota.py wipes it before the module runs so 'fresh store' assertions are deterministic — if you re-run just this file, expect the store to end again with the test 1.2.0 firmware. RadarCard on Summary uses RainViewer public radar tiles + ESRI base tiles which DO load from the preview server (verified via screenshot showing NY/NJ coastline). Setting a ZIP requires typing into the 'ZIP code' TextInput on the Flights tab (placeholder '28117') and pressing Enter — there is no explicit Apply button; geocoding takes ~3-5s.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no defect detected. All acceptance criteria in the review request produced the expected observable behavior.
